attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He states them as his own expectation.

semantics.note: 'I expect' is an unqualified expectation, and 'won't' is firm, so this is a scored forecast. The proposition captures both parts: the ordering of physical before psychological reasoning, and no single AGI arrival day. No deadline was given; 2062 is only an example.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: meaningful gains, not human-level competence, with the two parts assessed separately and no deadline. It treats the 2062 date as illustrative. It is not stretched for or against Marcus.

evidence.note: Google's own 2023 report of RT-2 gains on unseen tasks. It shows embodied improvement but not that it came before any psychological-reasoning gain.
A January 2026 preprint finding more robust theory-of-mind performance. It does not date the first psychological gain relative to physical gains.
A September 2026 assessment finding the published evidence insufficient to call GPT-6 Astra AGI. There is no established abrupt or completed arrival, so no conclusive event.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet has isolated advances in both areas but no comparable dated chronology showing which improved first. No AGI transition, abrupt or gradual, has been established. The early-resolution rule is not met, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He asserts the funding point in his own voice, framed as agreeing with Booch.

semantics.note: Reading 'not going' as a typo for 'now going' is reasonable, since he calls LLMs a distraction. The 'seems like' judgment stays as opinion. The checkable part is the current funding share.

contract.note: Limiting the money to funding aimed at general intelligence and reading 'most' as a majority by value is an ordinary reading in context. The January window was chosen by the evaluator, but it counts existing allocations, which softens that choice. The verdict does not turn on these choices because the evidence settles nothing.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure of its April 2022 round. It is one company in a different period and gives no portfolio share.
The Stanford AI Index total for 2022 covers all private AI investment. Its period and scope differ, and it has no split by LLM.
A January 2023 report of unconfirmed Microsoft investment talks. It shows no completed allocation and gives no denominator.

reviews.rationale: Testing the claim needs the total funding aimed at general intelligence in early 2023 and the share that went to LLMs. The packet has only single funding rounds, unconfirmed talks, and an all-AI total for a different year. None of these establishes or rejects a majority share, so the claim is unresolved.
